text:
maria: Heads up — we're seeing a p99 latency spike in us-east-1 at ~18:10. Correlates with a sharp drop in prefix cache hit-rate after this morning's config push (kv.eviction_target lowered). digging now.

aj: Can you paste the metric snippets? which rollout triggered it?

maria: Rolling window: prefix_hit_rate 92% -> 14% over 2 mins; eviction_rate 0.8/s -> 45/s; p99 tokens/req went from 90ms -> 420ms.

sylvia: Did we also flip the batching heuristic or kernel selection in the same deploy? I remember land of batcher max_seq change yesterday.

maria: Checking deploy tags... looks like config change 2026-03-18T09:02 (kv.eviction_target=0.2) + runtime tweak attn-kernel `auto-select=experimental-v2` got enabled in canary and rolled.

aj: paste quick snippets (logs or grafana panels).

maria: paste: ```
# metrics snapshot (us-east-1/pool-a)
prefix_hit_rate: 0.14
kv_evictions_per_s: 45
p50_latency_ms: 31
p95_latency_ms: 210
p99_latency_ms: 422
throughput_rps: -12% vs baseline
```

runtime-oncall: Scoped it — I temporarily set kv.eviction_target=0.5 for pool-a and pinned kernel to `attn-stable` on the nodes serving that pool. Restarting worker pods now.

infra-bot: deploy started: redeploy/kv-config-pool-a by runtime-oncall (job id 8492).

deploy-bot: rollout complete: kv-config rollback -> kv.eviction_target=0.5 (9 of 9 pods updated).

maria: After rollback: prefix_hit_rate climbed back to ~70% within 40s, p99 back down to ~120ms. We still saw an eviction wave that wiped hot prefixes.

sylvia: Observed during profiling: batcher change led to longer prefix keys staying in-memory less predictably. Combined with the lower eviction_target the LRU scanner started evicting by size not recency because of a kernel-level memory layout change (experimental-v2 puts KV slab metadata in a different place). That caused an unintended increased churn.

aj: So root cause is interplay of three things: eviction_target config, batching heuristic (longer seqs), and kernel selection layout change. Any evidence of noisy tenant causing pressure?

maria: Good catch — logs show a tenant `adprod-42` with a burst of ~12k short-unique prefixes in ~30s (ad requests generating many new prefixes). That coincided with the eviction wave.

sylvia: That looks like a noisy neighbor + poisoning pattern: many ephemeral prefixes -> cold inserts -> pushes out hot prefixes when eviction target low + different slab layout made eviction less LRU-friendly.

maria: Quick excerpt from worker perf/top and eviction log: ```
[evict] epoch=1612 scans=4800 evicted=12645 top-evict-keys=adprod-42_*
perf: cpu cycles spent in slab_reclaim: 72%
```

ops: Can we add a short term mitigation besides rollback? e.g., tenant throttle or per-tenant reserve?

sylvia: Short term: enable per-tenant reservation (10% weight to each tenant) on pool-a and add a prefix normalization that hashes long dynamic prefixes into limited buckets. I'll sketch the patch.

runtime-oncall: Alerts adjusted: create alert if prefix_hit_rate < 30% for 1m AND p99 > 200ms. Also adding eviction_rate > 5/s.

aj: We should capture heap/kv histogram and a perf profile for the experimental kernel. Can someone open an incident ticket? I will own the postmortem.

maria: I'll attach flamegraphs and the worker heap snapshot to the ticket.

infra-bot: ticket created: INF-7243 "prefix cache hit-rate collapse after kernel+config rollout" assigned to eng-runtime and eng-ml.

ops: Action items: 1) sylvia - propose per-tenant reserve + prefix normalization patch (ETA 4h). 2) runtime-oncall - add alerts + canary pinned kernel flag (done). 3) aj - postmortem doc + timeline (ETA EOD). 4) maria - attach perf artifacts.

maria: Also adding a unit test for eviction policy under slab layout change so we don't regress.

sylvia: For the long term: we should add a kernel-level contract for KV slab metadata layout so the eviction scanner stays LRU-consistent across kernel variants. I'll create a design doc.

aj: Great. TL;DR: cause = config + batching + kernel selection + noisy tenant. Rollback + per-tenant throttles mitigated. Postmortem to follow. :white_check_mark:

maria: Thank you all. Leaving monitoring pinned on pool-a for 24h.

runtime-oncall: I'll keep an eye, will escalate if hit-rate dips again.

ops: Please add owners to the incident doc and link any PRs.

maria: Will do. End of thread.
